MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 28, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting
was conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the
City Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public
comments that were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:01 p.m., on April 28, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 23, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project
  v. The City of Mission Viejo.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned the City Attorney and City Council regarding alternative
remedies to the City's election code violations and expressed concerns of collusion. She stated

City Council Minutes  1  April 28, 2020
 that the voters of Mission Viejo were not given an opportunity to voice their position on district-
based elections versus cumulative voting.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:12 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that despite an earlier public comment which seemed to
indicate that City staff and the City Council are mishandling the voting rights actions and
upcoming election, that is not the case. He stated that the Council and staff are acting in complete
compliance with the law and that there has been no collusion or mischief. Under the Mayor’s
leadership the City has been working with the Secretary of State and although his office originally
said that there was no path for a general law city to look to cumulative voting, after discussion and
interaction there in fact may be. The Secretary of State is withholding any certain final judgement
but has indicated that the City is available to present to him and his staff the path that Mission
Viejo sees as viable. The Secretary of State will review and work with the City in good faith,
perhaps giving suggestions or at least their reactions. City Attorney Curley noted that it is good
news that they are willing to review, give guidance, advice and suggestions and staff will work to
come up with a plan to implement it, certainly subject to the Secretary of State’s final decision.
The City will continue with the issue of the litigation and stipulated judgement.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

M.D.: Stated that 80% of Californians believe the state should stay under COVID-19 quarantine
and not submit to the other 15-20% that don’t believe so. She feels that California has been
successful because of its actions.

DEPARTMENT HEAD UPDATES REGARDING COVID-19 ACTIVITIES

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay

Public Services is continuing to provide essential services throughout the City. These include: pool
maintenance, landscape maintenance, street sweeping, trash collection, tree trimming for safety,
irrigation management, and pothole repairs after the extensive rain last week. Public Services
wants the community to know that the City’s open spaces and parks are open, including the public
restrooms. The restrooms continue to be cleaned, wiped down and disinfected daily. Public
Services staff has continued to monitor the social distancing signage and play area safety tape to
visually communicate that various park elements are closed during the Stay at Home Order. These
signs encourage adherence to the social distancing standards by the CDC to clearly let the
community know that playgrounds are closed for use during this time. Animal Services staff
continue to provide full level of services. Most are being provided through online resources and/or
by appointment. The Animal Services team produced an in-house volunteer recognition video to
keep volunteers engaged during the current mandates. Building Services has implemented
additional facility cleaning and disinfecting operations at each of the City’s various sites. These
focus on increased restroom deep cleaning to three times per day; upstaffing to have janitors focus
on good, sound cleaning and disinfecting of high-touched surfaces such as door handles, light
switches, hand rails, elevator buttons, sinks and faucets, restroom stalls and dispensers, vending
machines and counter tops; all tables and chairs used in meeting rooms and banquet rooms are
being disinfected and tagged (Norman P. Murray Community Center/Saddleback Room); and
added nightly cleaning in the Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) office at The Shops at
Mission Viejo and all OCSD remote sites. City staff have been scheduled to work full time on
upkeep of buildings and facilities during the shutdown. These include repair and painting walls,
deep cleaning of carpeted areas and cleaning of all storage areas. Staff is specifically moving
forward to paint the interior of various rooms in the community center and to advance the flooring
reorder so that the flooring throughout the Center can be replaced during the closure. City staff
have been working on the golf club house too: painting the interior and exterior of the facility,
City Council Minutes  4  April 28, 2020
 deep cleaning and replacing old fixtures and furniture. Staff have been working on rehabilitating
the on-course pump house, installing enhanced technology throughout the building, aerating the
greens, automating irrigation systems, and slurry and stripping the parking lot, all in an effort to
prepare for the reopening of the facility this coming Friday May 1, 2020. The facility will re-open
at 6:00 a.m. with the first tee time and will close daily at 7:00 p.m. City staff encourage the
community to check the course website for the defined opening procedures and he said we
welcome the golfing community back.

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas

The Administrative Services department continues to be fully functional with no disruption to
operations. This includes providing support to vendors, residents and other department operations.
A significant amount of time in the last few weeks has been dedicated to developing the budget
reduction plan for fiscal year 19/20 which is the next discussion item on the agenda. Staff have
already started a review of the fiscal year 20/21 budget. This review will take up a significant
amount of time over the next four to six weeks and new revenue projections should be available
by the end of this week or early next week. Director Dyas said that knowing the appropriation
budget will help with reduction goals for next year and staff plans to bring an amended fiscal year
20/21 budget to Council on June 23, 2020. Risk Management staff have started working on return
to work policies with the utmost importance on providing the best protection possible to staff and
members of the public who will visit City facilities once they start opening to the public. Director
Dyas reminded people that COVID-19 continues to present a risk to all members of the public and
will continue to do so for many more months to come.

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister

Looking just at the Building Division (not including Planning) from April 1 through April 24,
2020, 150 building permits were issued, 590 inspections were conducted, 540 telephone calls, and
2,623 emails were received. In regards to the Planning Department Shea’s Neo and Haven Projects
are moving forward with 105 residential units. They anticipate pulling their first building permit
for the homes on July 20, 2020, with last building permit being pulled November 21, 2020.
Trumark Homes has submitted a plan for 91 town home units on the Saddleback Church site and
an RFP for the Golf Course Visioning Plan is due back to the City on May 6, 2020. Director Lister
noted that department staff have also been working with the Chamber of Commerce on a restaurant
survey and responses are due back Friday. Lastly, the City will receive an additional $225,000 in
CBDG COVID-19 funds and staff is looking at different options at this time, such as business
support, and will present ideas to the Economic Development Committee.

Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander

It’s now been over 6 weeks since Information Technology (IT) set up essential staff to work
remotely and there are more than 110 workers conducting all City business remotely from home.
An additional 239 staff members are set up with access to their email and to the City’s financial
system to access timesheets and payroll information. IT’s helpdesk is busy responding to
essentially the same types of requests and problems users encountered in the office. A small
percentage of staff does come in to the office to conduct manual duties and some printing but the
majority conduct all their business from home and can fully function remotely. Departments
continue to schedule coverage in the office so IT does support staff - both on premise at City Hall
and remotely. They continue to maintain, patch and update, all the desktop computers that are in
City Council Minutes  5  April 28, 2020
 the office including the public computers located at the library and the laptops issued to the remote
workforce. In addition, IT is supporting staff while at home using their personal computers.
Director Alexander said that about one third are using their home computers and this takes
additional support and security setup to maintain. IT staff continue to support the infrastructure
which includes servers, storage, network equipment, building security, audio visual systems
among other things so it is helpful to have an IT staff person scheduled daily to serve as the “hands-
on” person for the team while the rest of the IT team works remotely. The security work of patching
systems with the latest software updates to secure our network is ongoing so they have added some
new security protocols to assist with the changing and increasing security threats. Director
Alexander said that everyone likely heard that last month the City of Torrance had a ransomware
attack that crippled the City’s email, website, and all data for several weeks. The hackers requested
100 bitcoins and then proceeded to essentially blackmail the City by releasing data online to force
the City to pay. These types of attacks are rampant and Mission Viejo’s IT department does a
tremendous amount of work to prepare for such security threats. The work to maintain and secure
our network is invisible to most but it is continuous, challenging, and takes a great effort to conduct
and maintain by the IT team. Staff is also involved in supporting all departments with a variety of
their projects and events. IT was honored to be able to implement the technology to hold a virtual
International Holocaust Remembrance Day with dedicated email and call in line, broadcasting it
live and simultaneously to Cox TV, AT&T UVerse, YouTube and the City website. Staff is
currently preparing to securely accept photos from residents online to assist the Community
Relations department in honoring Mission Viejo graduates for their accomplishments. IT works
closely with the Community Relations department to assist them with preparing eNewsletters and
posting to social media as they effectively keep the community up-to-date. There are several
projects underway at Casta del Sol Golf Course including adding high speed internet access, Wi-
Fi, reviewing a GPS technology, and developing a new website. Also, IT published an RFP for
purchase of a land management system including permitting and plan checking. The RFP due date
is May 20, 2020, at which time the purchase of a new system will be evaluated. There are several
other projects underway addressing security, infrastructure and programs supporting the
departments and community that she didn’t go into but they are published on the IT departments
web page on the City’s site at https://cityofmissionviejo.org/IT.

Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman

The Community Relations department is continuing to respond to a large variety of public inquires
via email, phone calls and direct messages on social media. Staff is not only responding during
business hours but also on the weekends and evenings as necessary. The department is maintaining
a robust public information campaign for COVID-19 through the City’s social media platforms,
the weekly eNewsletter which is distributed to nearly 30,000 subscribers, and on the dedicated
COVID-19 web page (cityofmissionviejo.org/COVID-19). Staff have been filming popular video
message with Mayor Goodell each week. Last week he was joined by two special guests, his dogs
Max and Lucy, who are adoptees from the Mission Viejo Animal Services Center. In the video,
Mayor Goodell outlined the ongoing services that are being offered at the animal shelter during
the pandemic. Mission Viejo Television had the distinct honor of filming Holocaust Survivor Max
Silberberg last week on Holocaust Remembrance Day. Director Hamman thanked the Recreation
and Community Services Department for working with the Jewish Federation & Family Services
to arrange Mr. Silberberg’s time with MVTV and gave special thanks to Council Member Sachs
for stepping in at the last minute to host the presentation. For those who missed the live production,
the video is available in perpetuity on the City’s YouTube Channel at YouTube.com/
MissionViejoCA. The Community Relations department has also been working with Recreation
City Council Minutes  6  April 28, 2020
 and Community Services staff to create a Virtual Memorial Day Ceremony. The video will be
aired on MVTV and YouTube on Memorial Day in lieu of the City’s traditional live ceremony.
Lastly, the department has been helping Public Services by creating signage to outline the
guidelines for use of the Casta del Sol golf course in preparation for the reopening of the course
on Friday this week.

Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen

Last week, Library and Cultural Services staff made 1,766 wellness phone call checks for
volunteers, committee members and patrons and connected with 661 residents over age 65. The
calls were very well-received overall. Some common themes emerged from the conversations with
patrons: (1) there is strong interest in pickup/delivery services, (2) many people asked when the
Library will reopen, (3) many reported using the City and Library eNewsletters to stay informed,
and (4) overall people were happy to be called and appreciated what staff is doing. One person
who called back, said she loved that the City is checking in on residents and that we’re all heroes.
Staff is currently working on graduated plans for reopening that are adaptable to different levels
of restrictions with an emphasis on flexibility and being able to quickly transition between
restriction levels as guidance changes. Staff have prioritized planning logistics for contactless
curbside pickup and drop-off, as that will be the first phase of reopening procedures and will be in
high demand, based on feedback from patrons so far. Library staff continue with customer service
shifts: checking in books from the book drop, answering calls and emails, and creating new digital
library card accounts so that patrons can access online resources. Acquisitions and Technical
Services staff worked on completing invoicing and cancelling orders in order to close out
remaining purchase orders and redirect budget to meet the revenue shortfall. Technical Services
staff also worked on receiving and processing the large number of ordered materials that had come
in while staff were on leave. Director Hansen said they continue moving forward on grant projects
so as not to lose the grant funding and mid-project narrative and financial reports were completed
and submitted to the State Library. Staff is working on draft plans for Arts and Library activities
and virtual programs that can be offered at no cost to the City. After the Holocaust Memorial
program, Council Member Sachs shared that he had been contacted by a number of people who
were interested in Mr. Silberberg’s book, so Library staff are working with Mr. Silberberg’s
daughter to make copies available.

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon

At the last update, Director Chagnon mentioned that permit activity was up as utility agencies and
contractors are taking advantage of reduced traffic conditions to perform construction in the public
right of way. To put some figures to that statement, Public Services issued 39 encroachment
permits in April of 2019. So far this month, they have issued 56 with several pending so almost a
50% increase. He also noted that staff is preparing a couple of its own large paving projects for
the summer. As an example of efforts to reduce costs, Public Works engineers are using their
design and computer drafting skills to prepare the plans in-house. This preserves about $50,000
which would typically be paid to a consulting firm. Public Works was recently notified by the City
of Rancho Santa Margarita (RSM) that it intends to renew the shared services agreement for solid
waste and water quality consulting for another year. Through this agreement, one of Mission
Viejo’s engineers spends 2 days a week at RSM which not only generates revenue for Mission
Viejo, but it promotes a good working relationship with our neighboring city. Mission Viejo
Country Club’s driving range has been undergoing a complete rehabilitation due to a failed storm
drain system running beneath it. Public Works has been coordinating with the Country Club on
City Council Minutes  7  April 28, 2020
 this effort and will be working closely with them in the coming weeks as construction of the new
storm drain system commences. Lastly, staff continue to work with the design consultant on the
plans for Lower Curtis Park and expect to have 75% of the design completed by the end of May
with the objective of having final plans later this year. The ongoing I-5 Widening project will be
generating large quantities of dirt which could potentially be used to create a rough-graded super-
pad at little or no cost to the City.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix

Although City facilities remain closed, the Recreation and Community Services Department
remains busy within the community. Hygiene Donation Program – since launching almost two
weeks ago staff has been able to collect $5,000 in donated products. These donations are being
split between Stand Up for Kids and OC Rescue Mission. In partnership with South County
Outreach, the City hosted a food drive at the Murray Center which collected approximately 3,300
pounds of non-perishable foods which will go to those in need. The City will solely host a food
drive again on May 2 at the Murray Center between 9 and 11 a.m. This food will be packaged into
bags and then picked up by those who need it within the community. The Recreation department
continues to see increases in its other food programs including the monthly commodities program,
weekly Park-It Market which distributes approx. 1,000 pounds of food each week, and the daily
Home Delivered Meals (HDM) program. With the increases for the HDM program, City staff have
assisted Agewell Senior Services to get these meals out. Staff alone distribute 233 meals each week
and in addition to these meals, staff prepared 119 bags of food which were given to individuals
enrolled in the HDM program to provide them some additional food while self-isolating. Since the
last meeting, the department has extended facility closures which resulted in processing 300
changes or reservation cancellations. There are another 1,000 reservations to go which includes
picnic shelters, field reservations, and facility rentals. Staff is also working with youth sports
groups and school districts to determine if they can accommodate summer programming and some
spring activities which were cancelled. 170 wellness check phone calls are conducted per day to
Murray Center participants, senior members, and those who have reached out to the City for this
service. These checks have been well received and staff have been able to connect people to
resources they need, particularly access to food for those seniors who don’t wish to leave their
home. The department is also finalizing re-opening plans and incorporating social distancing
measures for when the time comes to reopen recreational facilities. On April 21, the department
along with IT and Community Relations, hosted a virtual Holocaust Remembrance Day program
where Councilmember Sachs interviewed a 90-year old Holocaust survivor. Through the efforts
of MVTV this program was streamed live and filmed. Staff received a positive response and there
have been requests for copies of the program including those from teachers who wish to show the
program to their students. Lastly, the department is currently preparing for a virtual Memorial Day
Ceremony.

OLD BUSINESS

9.  Local Emergency for COVID-19 Update

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes updated the City Council with current
  information including the following.

  Due to the outbreak of the Corona Virus the City Council ratified and confirmed the City
  Manager’s Proclamation of a Local Emergency, which was initially declared by the City
City Council Minutes  8  April 28, 2020
   Manager on March 14, 2020. The City Council directed staff to provide updates at
  subsequent Council Meetings. As of today, April 28, 2020, there are approximately 2,151
  positive cases of COVID-19 in Orange County with cumulative deaths at 42. Statewide
  positive cases total 43,464 with deaths reaching 1,755. Nationally, positive cases exceed over
  one million with over 59,000 deaths. City Executive Management continue to meet in the
  City’s Emergency Operations Center, via teleconferencing three to four days per week. The
  County EOC Jurisdictional conference call has been scaled back to once per week. Over the
  past two weeks, hospital bed capacity has been running lower that average, ranging from
  46% to 54%. Updated information related to Orange County cases can be found on Orange
  County Health Care Agency’s website at https://occovid19.ochealthinfo.com. The Health
  Care Agency reports that COVID-19 testing continues to be focused on the seriously ill,
  medical response personnel and/or other essential personnel who are exhibiting systems.
  Members of the public at-large who are ill and exhibit symptoms are encouraged to call their
  medical provider to seek treatment options and inquire about testing based on their individual
  circumstances. As of April 21, 2020, additional testing sites are now being offered at several
  locations throughout Orange County (see exhibit B of staff report). These facilities offer
  FDA-approved COVID-19 testing to Orange County residents who have symptoms of
  COVID-19. This test identifies if a subject is currently infected based upon a sample taken
  with a swab. It is not a blood test, nor does it test for antibodies. Patients will receive a
  medical assessment before being tested and will only be tested if they are symptomatic. Early
  today a new blueprint for guidance on testing, including antibody testing, was released by
  the White House. The City will continue to stay in touch with the County health care officials
  to monitor the roll-out of any expanded testing programs. COVID-19 information is
  continuously posted to the City’s COVID-19 website and social media outlets to keep the
  public informed. This information can be found on the City’s website at
  cityofmissionviejo.org. On April 21, 2020, the County Board of Supervisors issued a
  directive related to the use of masks whereby certain employees at some essential businesses
  must wear face coverings (see exhibit C of the staff report). This directive stipulates “All
  employees of any grocery store, pharmacy/drug store, convenience store, gas station,
  restaurant, food preparation establishment, or retail store in Orange County who may have
  contact with the public must wear a cloth face covering while at work.” Also, on April 21,
  2020, the County Board of Supervisors approved guidance related to the safe operations of
  golf courses. This allows private and public courses to open if health and safety measures
  are put in place to mitigate the spread of COVID-19. The full list of these measures is
  specified in the County Minute Action attached as exhibit D. Lastly, regarding the personal
  protective equipment orders the City placed as emergency protective measures against
  COVID-19: as previously reported, staff placed orders for masks, gloves, and hand sanitizer
  to protect City employees and to distribute to identified high risk categories. In many cases
  initial orders were either delayed or cancelled by the distributors due stock shortages.
  Fortunately, over the last week the shipment of masks, gloves and hand sanitizer have been
  fulfilled. The City distributed masks and hand sanitizer to all City departments. Based on an
  outreach survey conducted by the Community Services Department staff will begin the
  distribution of supplies to some of the assisted living facilities that had communicated that
  they are running low on supplies. To date the City has received 750 bottles of hand sanitizer,
  775 cloth masks, 1,500 kn95 disposable masks, and 500 packets of gloves. There are an
  additional 2,500 kn95 disposable masks on order and staff will continue to distribute supplies
  as they are received.

11. Residential Building Permit Fee Waiver Program

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Council vote no.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that this proposal is unethical and asked the Council to vote no.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)

16. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum gave a shout-out to all the health care workers for their hard work and
to Mission Viejo residents for their common sense in social distancing while on the City’s trails.
She reminded residents to make sure their dogs are on leashes when out in public. Council Member
City Council Minutes  11  April 28, 2020
 Bucknum thanked Lieutenant Vuong for allowing her to go on a ride-along to honor resident
Chanel Dalirifar for her release from the hospital after suffering from COVID-19. As she
mentioned at the last meeting, Chanel was honored last year by the City Council for her heroic
deed in saving a person from committing suicide at The Shops at Mission Viejo. Lastly, Council
Member Bucknum complimented Lieutenant Vuong and noted that his deputies have nothing but
great things to say about Lt. Vuong’s leadership.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced the Chamber of Commerce meets via Zoom every week for
their Chamber breakfast and this morning they had 46 in attendance. The businesses share ideas
on how to stay afloat during this time. He announced that High Park Tap House is now open for
take-out and encouraged residents to buy from local businesses. Council Member Raths indicated
that tomorrow night the Chamber is hosting a Happy Hour via Zoom at 4:00 p.m. and anyone
interested can go to the missionviejochamber.com for information on how to attend. He mentioned
that he met with an elderly gentleman that had grown up in Nazi occupied Netherlands and he
compared the current pandemic to that time. The man expressed the importance of civil rights as
well as people’s rights under the Constitution and said that during his time in the Netherlands, the
common denominator was fear. Council Member Raths noted that the whole idea of self-seclusion
and to stay home is to ensure that the hospitals are not overflowing with patients. As Paul
Catsimanes’ report stated earlier, half the beds in Mission Hospital are empty. Council Member
Raths mentioned a video of two doctors from California who state that only .3% of people that
catch the virus die and those individuals have underlying health conditions or are elderly. He said
that he realizes, as more data is received, the City will need to evaluate it and figure out how to get
the City back up and running. In closing, Council Member Raths thanked Mayor Goodell for the
magnificent job he is doing along with a great City Council.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that it was an honor to be afforded the opportunity to interview
Holocaust Survivor Sam Silberberg and it is something that he will never forget. He said that City
staff are doing an extraordinary job under the conditions that the City is in. He noted that he’s also
glad to see that complaints are down from residents who don’t like the directional restrictions on
the walk around the lake. Council Member Sachs thanked the City Manager and staff for all their
work as well as Mayor Goodell. In closing, he said that he misses public comments and seeing
people at the podium in the Council Chamber and looks forward to when the Council can return
to City Hall for meetings.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that we are in different times and she usually has so much to report,
but everything has been cancelled. She commended Mayor Goodell on his regular updates and
videos, and for giving everyone hope. She also thanked various staff for their hard work along
with the City Manager. She reminded residents, especially those who are hurting through illness
or lost jobs, that the Council is thinking and praying for them. If there is anything needed, she
encouraged residents to please reach out to the City. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley shared that Mission
Viejo was recently recognized as the 8th safest city in California regardless of population. She
highlighted that during this time, staff is taking the opportunity to do some updates while City
facilities are closed. She also commended Council Member Sachs for his interview with Holocaust
City Council Minutes  12  April 28, 2020
 Survivor Mr. Silberberg and said that to hear his story really puts everything we are going through
into perspective. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that a former Community of Character
Committee Member, Mona, has developed a program called “Project Adam” which provides a free
tutoring service to all school age children in both school districts from age kindergarten through
high school and she encouraged parents to utilize the service. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley also asked
residents to support local businesses and noted that there is a new program from the Governor
where $66 in meals can be provided to seniors that are in a certain income bracket. She asked that
staff get the word out to the senior residents regarding this program. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
announced that the Character Word for April is service and what a great time to reflect on the
service of everyone from neighbors helping neighbors, firefighters, police officers, doctors, and
nurses. She closed by asking residents to continue to pray for first responders, those on the front
lines, America and for God to heal the land.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell congratulated Council Member Sachs on his great interview with Mr. Silberberg.
He announced that he received an email with the County-issued guidelines for reopening and noted
that the Economic Development Committee will have some good recommendations for moving
forward to get businesses back up in the very near future. He announced that he would close the
meeting tonight in memory of long-time resident Dick Latham and he shared some background on
Dick who became a U.S. Marine in 1945 and served sixteen years. His service took him all over
the world from sea duty to Terminal Island in San Pedro to Camp Pendleton and then to
Washington D.C. at the Marine Corp. Headquarters. Dick also served as Marine Guard Duty at
the U.S. Embassy in Rio De Janeiro where he met his wife who was also working at the Embassy.
In 1952 he went back to Camp Pendleton at the rank of Gunnery Sergeant and was sent to Japan
as a Combat Reserve before the Korean War ended. Dick Latham spent quite a bit of time in
service to the Country and when he returned from Japan, he joined the Veterans of Foreign Wars
at post 6024 and was an active member the rest of his life, including the Youth Activities Chairman
for 20 years.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:49 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting, in memory Dick Latham, to Tuesday, May 12, 2020, at
